name: Influence of AI Use on Creativity in a Speculative Design Process
description: Investigates how integrating AI tools into a speculative design workflow affects designer creativity. The study examines whether AI assistance enhances or constrains creative output by analyzing design artifacts and process metrics from participants using AI-augmented versus standard design workflows. Provides empirical evidence on the role of AI in expanding or fixating design exploration during early-stage speculative ideation.

name: Understanding Design Fixation in Generative Artificial Intelligence
description: Studies how generative AI systems exhibit and propagate design fixation — the tendency to repetitively produce similar design solutions anchored to the prompt. Analyzes output diversity and structural similarity in AI-generated concept sets, comparing AI fixation patterns to documented human designer fixation. Has direct implications for how generative AI tools should be prompted during ideation phases to avoid anchoring effects that reduce solution diversity.

name: Facilitating Identification of Ergonomic User Needs Through AI-Assisted Observation
description: Proposes an AI-assisted methodology for identifying ergonomic user needs from observational data. Uses computer vision or natural language processing to analyze user behavior recordings and extract ergonomic requirements, reducing researcher burden and improving reliability in early-stage human-centered need-finding. Evaluated against traditional manual observation methods on accuracy of identified user needs.

name: Human-GenAI Co-Design: Exploring Factors Impacting Trust Calibration
description: Investigates the factors that influence how designers calibrate their trust in generative AI co-design partners. Studies how AI output quality, explanation transparency, task context, and user experience level affect trust formation and maintenance during collaborative design sessions. Provides a framework for understanding and designing GenAI tools that support appropriate trust calibration in human-AI design collaboration.

name: Emulating Cognitive Style in Large Language Models
description: Explores whether large language models can replicate the cognitive styles of human designers, including associative, systematic, and divergent thinking patterns. Evaluates prompt engineering and in-context learning strategies for steering LLM outputs to match different designer cognitive profiles measured on established instruments. Contributes to understanding LLMs as adaptive design partners that can match individual designer working styles, with implications for personalized AI design tools.

name: TRIZ-GPT: An LLM-Augmented Method for Problem-Solving
description: Integrates TRIZ (Theory of Inventive Problem Solving) methodology with GPT-class large language models to augment engineering innovation. The system guides users through TRIZ contradiction matrices and inventive principles, using LLM-generated elaborations to bridge abstract TRIZ concepts to concrete engineering problems. Demonstrates how structured inventive problem-solving frameworks can leverage the broad domain knowledge of LLMs to produce more actionable solution directions than either TRIZ or LLMs alone.

name: A Task-Decomposed AI-Aided Approach for Generative Conceptual Design
description: Presents a structured AI framework that decomposes the conceptual design process into discrete subtasks — function identification, principle selection, and concept synthesis — each handled by specialized AI modules. The task decomposition enables generative AI to address complex, open-ended design problems more systematically than single-prompt approaches, producing conceptual solutions with higher feasibility and alignment with engineering requirements. Evaluated on mechanical design benchmark problems.

name: Conceptual Design Generation Using Large Language Models
description: One of the first systematic studies on using large language models (GPT-4-class) for mechanical and product conceptual design generation. Evaluates LLM-generated design concepts against human-generated baselines on novelty, feasibility, and variety metrics. Demonstrates that LLMs can produce competitive conceptual designs when given well-structured design problem specifications, and establishes evaluation protocols for comparing AI and human ideation performance in early-stage design.

name: Generative Pre-Trained Transformers for Biologically Inspired Design
description: Applies GPT-class language models to biologically inspired design (biomimicry) by leveraging the model's encyclopedic biological knowledge. Uses prompting strategies to elicit biological analogs for engineering functions, enabling designers to explore biomimetic inspiration more broadly than manual literature search allows. Validated against expert biomimicry practitioner outputs on function-to-biological-structure mapping tasks, demonstrating LLMs can serve as scalable biomimicry partners.

name: An Unsupervised Deep Learning Model to Discover Visual Similarity in Design
description: Develops an unsupervised deep learning approach to discover visual similarity patterns in design artifacts, particularly engineering sketches and concept drawings. The model learns compact visual embeddings without labeled training data using contrastive or reconstruction-based objectives, enabling similarity-based retrieval of design concepts and automatic clustering of design spaces. Applications include inspiring cross-domain design transfers and building analogy databases from patent and product archives.

name: Evaluating Crowdsourced Design Concepts with Machine Learning
description: Presents machine learning methods for automated evaluation of crowdsourced design concepts at scale. Trains classifiers to predict expert ratings of design creativity, feasibility, and novelty from concept descriptions and images, enabling rapid screening of large design concept databases. Addresses the scalability bottleneck in open innovation and crowdsourcing platforms where manual expert evaluation cannot keep pace with submission volume. Validated on real crowdsourced design datasets.
